title: Best Social Listening Tools With AI Sentiment Analysis (2026)
summary: Most sentiment scores only read captions and comments. Compare 7 social listening tools with AI sentiment analysis on what their models actually read in video.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** The best social listening tools with AI sentiment analysis in 2026 are Syncly Social, Meltwater, Sprinklr, Talkwalker, Brandwatch, YouScan, and Sprout Social. They differ less on whether they have AI and more on what the sentiment model reads: captions and comments only, or also the speech and on-screen text inside short-form video. For consumer brands on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts, that input decides whether the score is right.


Every platform on this list claims AI sentiment analysis. The input is what separates them. A creator says "this foundation oxidized in two hours" on camera while the caption reads "GRWM ✨". A caption-only model scores that post neutral or positive, and the complaint never reaches your dashboard.


This guide sets the criteria first, then compares seven platforms on what each vendor's own documentation says the model reads, how it handles video, and what it costs.


## What should AI sentiment analysis in social listening actually measure?


AI sentiment analysis in social listening should measure how people feel about a specific brand, product, or attribute, based on everything they said and showed, not only the text they typed. If you need the fundamentals first, start with[what AI sentiment analysis in social listening is](https://syncly.app/blog/what-is-ai-sentiment-analysis-social-listening) .


**Video-native sentiment analysis** : sentiment scoring that runs on the spoken transcript and on-screen text of a video, alongside its caption and comments, so the score reflects what the creator actually said and showed.


Use four criteria to evaluate any vendor:


1.


**Input text.** Does the model read captions and comments only, or also speech-to-text transcripts and on-screen text (OCR)?


2.


**Context and sarcasm.** Can it read "love how this broke after one use" as negative? Even vendors admit the limit: Meltwater writes that "sarcasm and irony remain difficult even for advanced tools" (Source:[Meltwater, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/sentiment-analysis-tools) ).


3.


**Aspect level vs overall.** "The shade range is great but the pump broke" holds two opinions. An overall score averages them away.


4.


**Noise and bot filtering.** Giveaways, spam, and unrelated keyword matches inflate positive sentiment. Filtering must happen before scoring, not after.


The first criterion matters most for consumer brands. Brandwatch reports that 80% of images featuring a brand's logo do not include a written mention of the brand (Source:[Brandwatch](https://www.brandwatch.com/guides/logo-recognition/) ). Short-form video adds speech and text overlays on top of that gap.


## Which social listening tools offer AI sentiment analysis in 2026?


They are ordered by how explicitly each vendor documents sentiment running on video content, the first criterion above. Every capability claim comes from the vendor's own site.


**1. Syncly Social**
Syncly Social is a video social listening platform. Its Conversation Insights reads "sentiment, themes, and brand context, all read automatically from the videos you're listening to" (Source:[Syncly, 2026](https://syncly.app/social/feature/conversation-insights) ). The input is speech-to-text, on-screen text, and captions, surfaced in a Sentiments tab per query. Syncly reports 3–4x data coverage compared with text-only tools, a Syncly product proof point rather than an independent benchmark (Source:[Syncly Social, 2026](https://syncly.app/social) ).


-


**Best for:** beauty, F&B, and fashion brands whose conversation happens on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts.


-


**Limitation:** built video-first, so teams needing deep news coverage will pair it with a media suite.


**2. Meltwater**
Meltwater positions its platform for "one view of sentiment across social, news, podcasts, and video" (Source:[Meltwater, 2026](https://www.meltwater.com/en/blog/sentiment-analysis-tools) ). Its engineering team says it transcribes YouTube, Reels, TikTok, and X video and makes transcripts "searchable and analyzable just like any article or social media post" (Source:[Meltwater Engineering, 2026](https://underthehood.meltwater.com/blog/2026/08/11/rethinking-speech-to-text/) ). It has offered logo detection in images since 2022 (Source:[Meltwater, 2022](https://www.meltwater.com/en/press-releases/meltwater-announces-ai-powered-visual-listening-and-company-search) ).


-


**Best for:** comms teams that need earned media and social in one place.


-


**Limitation:** its pages do not document whether sentiment reads on-screen text.


**3. Sprinklr**
Sprinklr claims "industry-best accuracy across sentiment, emotions, entity identification and text classification" (Source:[Sprinklr](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/consumer-intelligence/social-listening/) ). Its Video Intelligence product adds frame-level visual AI and decodes "voiceovers, sounds, and music trends" (Source:[Sprinklr](https://www.sprinklr.com/products/consumer-intelligence/video-intelligence/) ).


-


**Best for:** global enterprises running care, marketing, and listening on one suite.


-


**Limitation:** its pages do not document which text inside a video feeds the sentiment score.


**4. Talkwalker**
Talkwalker "adds sentiment information to all results" and says it "can even detect basic forms of sarcasm" (Source:[Talkwalker](https://www.talkwalker.com/sentiment-analysis) ). It also detects brands in images, in videos with product placements, and in audio content (Source:[Talkwalker](https://www.talkwalker.com/products/features/visual-speech-recognition) ).


-


**Best for:** teams that want broad source coverage plus visual brand detection.


-


**Limitation:** its pages do not document whether sentiment scores the speech it detects.


**5. Brandwatch**
Brandwatch's 2022 sentiment model delivered "around 18% better accuracy on average" and official support for 44 languages, and can "occasionally" see past sarcasm (Source:[Brandwatch, 2022](https://www.brandwatch.com/blog/data-science-behind-brandwatchs-new-sentiment-analysis/) ). Consumer Research adds Image Analysis and the Iris AI assistant (Source:[Brandwatch](https://www.brandwatch.com/products/consumer-research/) ).


-


**Best for:** insights teams running deep, historical research across many languages.


-


**Limitation:** the pages reviewed do not document sentiment on video transcripts.


**6. YouScan**
YouScan detects positive, neutral, and negative sentiment automatically (Source:[YouScan, 2026](https://help.youscan.io/en/articles/3839178-working-with-sentiment-in-youscan-s-analytics) ) and offers aspect-based sentiment that "automatically extracts aspects from social mentions, reviews, and forums" (Source:[YouScan, 2026](https://youscan.io/blog/aspect-based-analysis/) ). Its Visual Insights add-on analyzes images for brand logos (Source:[YouScan](https://youscan.io/visual-insights/) ). Our[YouScan alternatives comparison](https://syncly.app/blog/youscan-alternatives-for-2026-10-tools-compared-on-pricing-and-sentiment-accuracy) goes deeper.


-


**Best for:** mid-market teams that want aspect-level sentiment at a published price.


-


**Limitation:** the Visual Insights page documents images, not video.


**7. Sprout Social**
Sprout's Listening add-on lets teams "gauge consumer emotions through our Sentiment tracking and scoring model" (Source:[Sprout Social, 2026](https://sproutsocial.com/pricing/) ). Its Trellis AI agent answers listening research questions in plain language (Source:[Sprout Social](https://sproutsocial.com/features/social-media-listening/) ).


-


**Best for:** social teams that already publish and engage in Sprout.


-


**Limitation:** Listening is sold as an add-on, and its pages do not document video input.

Run one test on your own data instead. Pull 50 TikTok videos about your brand with neutral captions, have each vendor score them, then read the transcripts yourself. The closest match wins.


## Which sentiment analysis tool fits beauty, F&B, and fashion brands?


Beauty, F&B, and fashion brands need a sentiment analysis tool that reads video, because that is where their customers review products. The best social media sentiment analysis tools for consumer brands score speech and on-screen text, then break sentiment down by product attribute.


-


**Beauty.** Complaints hide in "get ready with me" videos. Test whether the platform flags "broke me out" when the caption is only hashtags. Our analysis of[TikTok comment sentiment in skincare](https://syncly.app/blog/tiktok-comment-sentiment-skincare) shows how much the comment layer adds.


-


**Food & beverage.** Taste tests carry the verdict in speech. You need attribute-level themes such as sweetness, texture, and price. Syncly Social's[video analysis](https://syncly.app/social/feature/video-analysis) layer transcribes that commentary before scoring.


-


**Fashion.** Fit and quality feedback shows up in try-ons and hauls. Look for OCR on text overlays and filtering that removes giveaways before scoring.


For platform choice on TikTok specifically, see the[TikTok social listening guide](https://syncly.app/blog/best-tiktok-social-listening-tool) .

## Key Takeaways


-


Every platform on this list offers AI sentiment analysis; the difference is what the model reads.


-


Captions and comments miss complaints that creators only say or show on camera.


-


No vendor publishes video sentiment accuracy, so test on your own videos.


-


Beauty, F&B, and fashion brands need speech, on-screen text, and attribute-level themes.


-


Only Sprout Social and YouScan publish prices; the rest are quote-based.


Sentiment is only as accurate as the text underneath it. A caption-only model gives a confident score on part of the conversation. Choose the platform that scores what customers actually say in video.
